basis: Developmental delay, intellectual disability and microcephaly define the syndrome; split hand occurs in 80-99% and radial hypoplasia in 30-79%.
Invasive Pseudomonas external-ear infection; temporal bone/skull-base osteomyelitis is a characteristic, common component.
Congenital cleft palate and mandibular hypoplasia define oral and facial skeletal involvement; each reported in 3/3 patients.
Benign follicular neoplasm arising in the thyroid gland.
Defined by isolated inherited hearing loss; syndromic neurological manifestations do not apply across this umbrella.
Developmental impairment, hypotonia and frequent seizures define neurological dysfunction; feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Osteogenesis imperfecta subtype defined by skeletal fragility.
Hereditary disorder defined by expansile lesions of bone; no supported extraskeletal involvement.
Inherited susceptibility to ovarian cancer; reproductive organs have no axis, and susceptibility does not establish damage elsewhere.
Purely psychiatric mood disorder without defined damage to an organ axis.
Cerebroretinal disease defines the syndrome; hepatic fibrosis and hypocellular marrow with pancytopenia each occur in 2/2. Osteopenia and GI bleeding omitted under cap.
Congenital fistula/pit associated with external-ear malformation.
Brain overgrowth, developmental disability and thoracic hypoplasia define the syndrome; reduced IgA in 11/11 supports humoral immune deficiency.
Holoprosencephaly, ectrodactyly and oral clefts define the syndrome; microphthalmia/ptosis occur in 80-99%. Endocrine frequency unknown; no direct lung lesion established.
Generalized lymphatic vascular malformation; chylothorax occurs in 20%. Splenomegaly alone does not establish blood-organ dysfunction; cellulitis is a separate infection.
Inherited platelet aggregation defect causing bleeding; bruising and mucosal bleeding do not establish separate skin or mucosal disease.
Tumours originate in cranial or spinal nerves; ocular involvement applies only to particular subtypes.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy; scoliosis in 2/2 assessed and brachydactyly in 2/4 support skeletal involvement. Isolated renal/cardiac findings lack robust frequency.
Deletion syndrome classified under syndromes with intellectual disability; supplied evidence does not establish another commonly damaged organ.
Inherited abnormal proinsulin processing/secretion; hyperglycemia is occasional and does not support additional organ involvement.
Cowden mucocutaneous hamartomas and GI polyposis are defining; structural thyroid lesions occur in roughly 50-70% of Cowden patients. Subtype-specific frequencies are limited.
Immunodeficiency with defining seizures and lung disease; hepatic injury in 12/15. Hemophagocytosis (6/15) and renal insufficiency (4/15) omitted under cap.
Spontaneous spinal cerebrospinal-fluid leakage causes intracranial hypotension and neurological dysfunction.
Benign adipose neoplasm situated within the cerebral hemisphere; location determines the axis.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; congenital atrial septal defect occurs in 3/10 (30%). Other extracerebral defects are isolated reports.
